'''Kálmán'''  is an ancient Germanic origin [[Hungarian people|Hungarian]] surname and male given name. Outside Hungary, the name occurs sometimes in the form '''Kalman'''. It was derived from the Germanic name:  [[Koloman]], [[Coloman]] or Kolman. The Germanic name Coloman has been used by Germans since the 9th century.

'''Kalman''' ({{Script/Hebrew|קלמן}} in Yiddish and Hebrew, occasionally spelled Calman in Roman letters) is also a Yiddish given name that is a short form of the Greco-Jewish name Kalonymos ({{Script/Hebrew|קלונימוס}}, meaning "beautiful name", a reference to a miracle worked in God's name). Sometimes the long form and short forms are used together, as in the compound name Kalman Kalonymos. A nickname for Kalman is in Yiddish Kalma or Kalme.

The Yiddish and Hungarian names are a convergence with separate origins (the Yiddish name first appearing in the Rhineland in the middle ages with the famed [[Kalonymos family]]).

People with the name Kalman or Kálmán include:

* [[Attila Kálmán]] (born 1968), Hungarian organist and pianist
* [[Dan Kalman]] (born 1952), American mathematician
* [[Emmerich Kálmán]] (1882–1953), Hungarian composer of operettas

* [[Oszkár Kálmán]] (1887–1971), Hungarian bass singer

* [[Tibor Kalman]] (1949–1999), Hungarian graphic designer
